h: Planning a full day on the Atlantic Highway
p: The Milky Way sits right on the A39, the road known locally as the Atlantic Highway, which makes it easy to find whether you're staying in Bideford, Clovelly or further along the coast. You'll need a car to get here, and it's worth arriving close to opening time on busy summer days to get settled before the crowds build.

Most families make a full day of it. There's enough going on that you can easily spend from morning to late afternoon without repeating yourself, especially if you plan around the show times. Bring layers, because North Devon weather can switch from sunshine to drizzle in a heartbeat, and the indoor areas are a big part of the appeal on wetter days.

With mixed ages, it helps to agree a rough plan in the car. Let each child pick a must-do ride or activity, slot in a show, then fill the gaps. Little ones will appreciate a break in the quieter areas, while older kids can go back for another go on their favourites.
A picnic is a good way to keep costs down, though there are food options on site if you'd rather not carry it all.

Clovelly, a few minutes down the road, is unlike anywhere else. It's a privately owned, car-free village where a steep cobbled street tumbles down to the harbour, and goods are still moved on sledges. You pay to enter via the visitor centre, and it's well worth it. Hartland Abbey and the rugged cliffs around Hartland Quay are close by for more dramatic scenery and coastal walks.
